53	            if message is None:

56	                continue

61	                continue
62	            if isinstance(content, list):
63	                for block in content:

66	                        print(f"{ts} {role} TEXT: {short(block.get('text',''), 500)}")
67	                    elif btype == "tool_use":
68	                        name = block.get("name")
69	                        print(f"{ts} {role} TOOL_USE {name}: {summarize_input(name, block.get('input'))}")
70	                    elif btype == "tool_result":

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude

Under a squash merge the branch's commit body *becomes* `main`'s permanent record, while the explanation of what was dropped, if it lives in a PR comment, is not carried by the squash at all. ## Report: growth-extract conversation-log review (4 sessions)

All four sessions are unattended Claudinite task-executor runs (issue→task→converge→close), not interactive dialogue, so there's no user-correction/misunderstanding signal in any of them — friction here is entirely in tool-use efficiency.

### Issue #224 — `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation`
**No durable lesson.** Clean, fast run: 08:56:03 → 08:58:48 (~2m45s), each step justified by its own read. One `curl` attempt to `knesset.gov.il` / `www.gov.il` was rejected by the egress proxy (`CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`) — per the task's own exclusion list this is a permission/egress denial, so it's a note for the human only, not a rule: the proxy is evidently blocking `.gov.il` hosts outright, which may be worth a human look if that's an unintended block.

### Issue #230 — `tidy-repo/tidy-issues`
**Signal type:** suboptimal action.
**Candidate rule:** When calling `mcp__github__search_issues` (or `issue_read`) just to locate one issue by title/number, always pass `fields`/`minimal_output` (or a tight `perPage`) rather than an unnarrowed query — an unnarrowed search regularly returns tens of thousands of characters and blows the token cap, forcing a save-to-file + ad hoc parsing recovery.
**Best-guess mechanism:** extend the existing declared PreToolUse advisory `github-list-without-fields` (already fires for `list_pull_requests`/`search_issues` elsewhere in this same window, see issue #223 below) so it reliably fires on every `search_issues`/`issue_read` call missing `fields`, or add prose in a GitHub-tooling pack reiterating the MCP server's own "use minimal_output" guidance.
**Evidence:** Two consecutive `search_issues` calls at 08:58:08.820 and 08:58:09.241 (no `fields`) both errored: *"result (96,051 characters across 1 line) exceeds maximum allowed tokens"* and *"(96,079 characters)"*. Recovery (writing/running two ad hoc `python3 -c` parse scripts against the saved dump files) ran until 08:58:35.593 — roughly **27 seconds** of pure recovery overhead for a query whose actual answer was one line (`114 Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues`).

### Issue #223 — `claudinite-growth/prose-to-checks-sweep`
**No durable lesson** on its own — clean run, 08:59:17 → 09:01:39 (~2m22s), nothing to convert (the only local pack's `RULES.md` was empty boilerplate). Notably the PreToolUse advisory `github-list-without-fields` *did* fire here for both `list_pull_requests` and `search_issues` calls without `fields` — confirming the check exists and works in this repo, which sharpens the #230/#222 finding: the same class of call blew past the token cap in two other sessions, so the check's coverage (or the agent's attention to its advisory) is inconsistent enough to be worth reinforcing, not something already fully solved.

### Issue #222 — `claudinite-growth/growth-dedup`
**Signal type:** suboptimal action (same family as #230).
**Candidate rule:** same as above, but for `mcp__github__issue_read` (`get` method) specifically — a `get` on an issue whose body/comments embed a large "canon window diff" is not exempt from the size problem just because it isn't a list/search call.
**Best-guess mechanism:** same as #230 — widen `github-list-without-fields`'s tool coverage to `issue_read`, or note in project GitHub-tooling guidance that any MCP GitHub read can overflow and should be sliced up front.
**Evidence:** `issue_read` (`get`, issue #222) at 09:01:06.752 errored: *"result (64,017 characters across 1 line) exceeds maximum allowed tokens... Use offset and limit... and jq"* — the tool's own error message suggests `jq`, but the agent instead wrote three separate `python3 -c` one-liners (09:01:10.876, 09:01:22.719, 09:02:07.066) against the saved dump to get a line count, print one comment, then a string length — reaching the needed number only at 09:02:08.539, roughly **62 seconds** spread across the session on ad hoc parsing that a single `jq` filter (as the tool suggested) would have done in one shot.

### Summary
Two of four sessions (#230, #222) hit the identical friction — an unnarrowed GitHub MCP read/search overflowing the token cap — costing ~27s and ~62s respectively in recovery, with the fix (`fields`/`minimal_output`, or `jq` as the tool itself suggests) already present in tooling guidance but not applied. The other two sessions (#224, #223) are already optimal — no measurable waste, no misunderstanding, no rework.

## Report

**Issue 231** (tidy-prs task, 08:59:56–09:04:37Z, ~4.5 min): Clean, single-pass execution — claimed the item, read the task spec, assessed all 3 open PRs via git diff/log against fetched branches, found no state change needed, converged and closed. No backtracking, no redundant calls, no waits. **No durable lesson** — already optimal.

**Issue 228** (wiki-growth task, 08:59:35–09:14:10Z, ~14.5 min across both files): Also a clean unattended run overall — research, wiki edits, commit, PR, auto-merge, converge. One notable finding, plus a note (not a lesson) on a recurring denial pattern.

---

**1. Suboptimal action — stale local `main` broke the merge-policy check on first try**

- Signal type: suboptimal action (redundant work from a knowable stale ref)
- Candidate rule: before running `merge-policy.mjs --base <branch>` for a delivered PR, fetch and pass the freshly-fetched ref (e.g. `FETCH_HEAD` or `origin/<base>`) rather than the bare local branch name, which can be stale in this checkout model.
- Mechanism guess: this is canon plumbing (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md` / `merge-policy.mjs`), not local-repo-specific — flagging for canon rather than `local/packs/hitbut`. Best fix is probably in `merge-policy.mjs` itself (auto-fetch the base) or a stronger instruction in `deliver-pr.md`.
- Evidence: local `main` ref was at `375bc8c` while `origin/main` (and the checked-out branch) was already at `c78c95e`. First call:
  ```
  09:09:46.974 merge-policy.mjs --base main → huge bogus "uncovered" list over the whole repo
  09:09:58.165 git fetch origin c78c95e...
  09:10:10.586 merge-policy.mjs --base FETCH_HEAD → correct "AUTOMERGE: yes"
  ```
  Cost: ~25 seconds and one extra diagnose-and-rerun round trip (09:09:46.974 → 09:10:12.295). Small in isolation, but reproducible on every `deliver-pr` flow in any repo where the local `main` branch isn't kept fresh.

**2. Wall-time — already optimal**

The one wait in the session (PR #235's CI checks) was handled correctly: a blind `sleep 90` was blocked by the harness, the agent switched to `ScheduleWakeup` + a backgrounded `sleep 150`, and the check-run poll that followed found all 4 checks already `completed` — no idle time wasted, no re-polling an already-green check repeatedly. No fix needed here.

**Note for the human, not a lesson (recurring denial — per instructions, not written up as a rule to route around):** During wiki research, essentially every `WebFetch` call hit `EGRESS_BLOCKED` — 9 distinct domains across ~4 minutes (09:02:42–09:06:16Z): `knesset-ai.com`, `knesset.gov.il`, `archive.org`/`web.archive.org`, `fs.knesset.gov.il`, `restofworld.org`, `timesofisrael.com`, `en.wikipedia.org`, `globes.co.il`, `credibilitycoalition.org`. Not one `WebFetch` succeeded in this session; the agent worked around it entirely via `WebSearch` snippets, which is why the wiki edits landed cited only to search-result text rather than fetched page content. This is a sandbox/proxy policy boundary (per the web-scraping pack's own guidance: "don't route around it"), so it's not a candidate rule — just worth a human's attention if wiki-growth research is expected to fetch real page content going forward.

No misunderstanding-type signals in either log — both are unattended automation runs (routine-fire payloads) with no human back-and-forth to analyze.

## Summary

All three sessions are Claudinite task-queue executor runs (issues 148, 145, 152), following the same `queue/instructions.md` script. Two friction patterns recur identically across all three logs (strong, repeated evidence); one session (152) surfaces a distinct, costly bug in a task's own precondition. All the fixable code lives under vendored `.claudinite/shared/` — canon-owned, not this repo's local pack — so mechanism suggestions below point upstream rather than at `local/packs/hitbut/RULES.md`.

### Cross-log finding 1 — `converge-item.mjs`'s first call is a guaranteed failure
**Signal type:** suboptimal action (recurs 3/3 sessions, identical shape)
**Candidate rule:** Queue instructions should state up front that `converge-item.mjs` requires `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_REPO`/`CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON` to be set before the first invocation, not left for the agent to discover via a failed call.
**Mechanism:** canon fix to `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md` (or the script's own usage message) — out of scope for this repo's local pack.
**Evidence:** Every session runs `converge-item.mjs --issue N --outcome …` bare, gets `Exit code 2 … no repository — pass GITHUB_REPOSITORY or CLAUDINITE_ITEM_REPO`, then writes a scratch JSON file and retries with the env vars set. Issue 148: fails at `09:26:12.015`, retried by `09:26:23.993` (write) → `09:26:25.311` (result). Issue 145: fails `09:26:23.668`, JSON written by `09:26:35.379`. Issue 152: fails `09:28:47.546`, JSON written `09:29:02.405`, retried `09:29:10.512`. Same failure, same recovery, three times.

### Cross-log finding 2 — engine script paths are rediscovered by trial-and-error every session
**Signal type:** suboptimal action (recurs in all 3 logs)
**Candidate rule:** Point directly at the actual paths (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/converge-item.mjs`, `.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs`) from `queue/instructions.md` rather than a script name/pattern the agent must locate.
**Mechanism:** canon prose fix, same file as above.
**Evidence:** Issue 148 guessed `**/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs` via Glob (`09:24:33`, "No files found") before a broader `**/converge-item*` succeeded. Issue 145 guessed `find … -path "*/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs"` (`09:26:12.677`, empty result) before broadening. Issue 152 hardcoded `.claudinite/shared/hooks/session-end-command.mjs` for the session-end step, which actually **crashed** (`Cannot find module`, `09:29:25.856`) before a `find -iname` located the real path at `.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs` (`09:29:27.315`).

### Issue 152 — the improve-comments occurrence was structurally impossible
**Signal type:** wall-time waste + suboptimal precondition, well-measured
**Candidate rule:** `tidy-repo/improve-comments`'s window-selection precondition (`task.mjs`, "slices touchedPaths with no filter") should exclude paths under `.claudinite/shared/` before ever creating an occurrence, since those files can never legally be edited (`claudinite-lifecycle` rule: never edit vendored content).
**Mechanism:** canon fix to `.claudinite/shared/packs/tidy-repo/tasks/improve-comments/task.mjs`'s precondition filter.
**Evidence — measured:** session start `09:23:48.228`; the agent spends the bulk of the run (from `09:25:16` reading `.gitignore`/gitmodules checks through `09:28:38.823`, roughly **3m23s**) verifying that all 40 handed-off files sit under the vendored tree, then posts the failure comment at `09:29:19.888` — **≈5m32s total, zero actionable work**, because the occurrence could never have succeeded. Quote: "every one of the 40 files in this occurrence's Context sits under the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` tree… and this repo's own `claudinite-lifecycle` rule is unambiguous."

### Issue 145 — secondary note
**Signal type:** suboptimal action (minor)
**Evidence:** `get_comments` returned a comment 60,603 chars long, tripping the token cap (`Error: result … exceeds maximum allowed tokens`, `09:25:02.720`); the agent then spent 3 extra Bash/python round-trips (`09:25:09.923`→`09:25:29.941`, ~20s) to selectively parse the saved file and skip the oversized comment. Not worth a standalone rule; folds into finding 2's theme (queue-issue comment volume growing unbounded) but too thin on its own to recommend a fix.

**Net:** no local-pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/hitbut/RULES.md`) rule is warranted from any of the three — every well-evidenced finding points at canon-owned files (`claudinite-tasks` queue scripts, `tidy-repo`'s precondition). Recommend filing these as upstream Claudinite issues rather than editing this repo.
